question: Directly asking a patient about suicidal thoughts or intent increases the likelihood that they will attempt suicide.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Clinical evidence and professional guidelines confirm that directly asking about suicidal ideation does not increase suicide risk. Many patients report feeling relieved when a clinician asks — it signals that the topic is safe to discuss. Failure to ask directly is a significant missed-assessment error.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Research consistently shows that directly asking about suicidal ideation does not increase risk. On the contrary, sensitive, non-judgmental inquiry opens the door to disclosure and safety planning. Avoidance of the question is one of the most dangerous clinical errors in suicide risk assessment.
